content.title: About
content.content: Plantain chips are thin slices of ripe or green plantain that are fried or baked until crisp. The plantain (Musa paradisiaca) is a tropical fruit related to the banana, widely cultivated in Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia. The chips have a mildly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture, often used as a healthier alternative to potato chips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Plantains are one of the most calorie‑dense fruits but also provide a lot of dietary fiber.
Unlike bananas, plantains are usually cooked before eating – boiled, fried or baked.
Plantain chips are popular in Caribbean and African cuisines, served as snacks or side dishes.
Plantains are rich in resistant starch, which acts as a prebiotic and supports gut health.
There are two main types of chips: made from ripe (sweet) and green (savory) plantains.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Plantains provide vitamin B6 and B3, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains resistant starch
items.content: Resistant starch is not digested in the small intestine but fermented by gut bacteria, fostering beneficial microbes.

items.title: Lower sugar in green form
items.content: Green plantain chips have a lower glycemic index compared with typical potato chips.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Plantain chips are rich in fats and calories, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Allergy to banana family
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to plantains, reacting similarly to bananas.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salted versions can contain significant amounts of sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Aflatoxin risk if stored improperly
items.content: Storing in warm, humid conditions can promote mold growth that produces aflatoxins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Plantain chips can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, soups, or used as a crunchy topping for dishes. They are often served with yogurt‑based dips, avocado, or spicy chili sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any chips that develop a rancid smell or off‑flavor.
